exactDelta.changeSummary: States the positive connected-generator-terminal premise before the experiment; states that leaf angle does not distinguish polarity; concludes decreasing absolute potential toward ground; conditions signed decrease on positive polarity and explicitly gives signed increase for a negative terminal.

freshAffectedSCI.originalDefect: Polarity-insensitive leaf deflection was used to infer an unconditional decrease of signed potential from an unspecified generator terminal toward ground.
freshAffectedSCI.magnitudeVersusPolarity: In the described comparable-foil demonstration, reversing all apparatus charges preserves repulsion because Q1 Q2 = (-Q1)(-Q2). The same qualitative angle pattern therefore cannot identify the sign of potential relative to ground. The inserted qualifier correctly limits the angle observation to magnitude rather than polarity.
freshAffectedSCI.signedPotentialDerivation: Let x increase from generator to ground, R > 0 be strip resistance and r(x) its cumulative resistance from the generator. In the already specified ordinary settled conductor with negligible lead drop, V(x) = Vg[1-r(x)/R] and I_x = Vg/R. Absolute potential decreases toward ground for either sign of Vg. Signed potential decreases toward ground only when Vg > 0; for Vg < 0 it increases toward zero. This checks the corrected experimental conclusion, not a new review of the unchanged ordinary-conduction lesson.
freshAffectedSCI.positivePremisePlacement: The corrected text explicitly chooses the connected electrode to be positive relative to ground before describing either circuit state, and repeats that premise immediately when asserting a decrease of signed potential. Its opening comparison of leaf angles is therefore qualified within the same complete changed unit.
freshAffectedSCI.originalCounterexampleRetested: For a uniform strip connected to -100 V, signed potentials from generator through midpoint to ground are -100, -50 and 0 V, while magnitudes are 100, 50 and 0 V. The leaves still show decreasing deflection, but signed potential rises. The corrected final sentence explicitly states that rise and no longer contradicts this counterexample.
